prompt:
A single Japanese yonkoma manga page, one continuous image divided into a grid of panels with thin black panel borders. Clean bold black ink outlines, flat cel-shaded colors with soft muted palette, expressive chibi-proportioned characters, gentle lighting, lightly comedic mood with a hint of eerie SCP Foundation atmosphere (concrete corridors, fluorescent lights, containment facility props).

This single image is a 2x2 grid of 4 manga panels, arranged left-to-right then top-to-bottom.

Characters appearing across these panels (keep designs exactly consistent in every panel):
- Dr. Hana, a young female SCP Foundation researcher in her late 20s. Chin-length straight black bob hair, thin round glasses, calm slightly tired eyes. Wears a plain white lab coat over a dark navy turtleneck, with a blank white ID card clipped to the chest pocket. Slim, average height.

Panel 1 (top-left): Wide shot, full body, eye level, showing Dr. Hana's whole desk and office from a slight side angle during a quiet moment. She sits idly flipping through a thick hardcover book, reading with mild curiosity, one finger tracing a line of text on the open page.

Panel 2 (top-right): Close-up shot centered tightly on Dr. Hana's face, filling most of the frame: she jolts upright, one hand flying to her own mouth, shoulders hiccuping visibly, eyes wide with surprise, the open book just a blurred sliver at the bottom edge of the frame.

Panel 3 (bottom-left): Medium shot, waist-up, wide two-shot composition with the doorway on one side and the desk on the other. A concerned coworker leans into the office doorway, tilting his head with a puzzled expression at Dr. Hana across the room, who is still hiccuping and pointing guiltily with one hand at the book lying open on her desk.

Panel 4 (bottom-right): Wide shot, full body, symmetrical composition with Dr. Hana on one side and the coworker mirrored on the other, both standing and hiccuping in unison, shoulders jerking at the same time, staring at each other with wide startled eyes, while the encyclopedia sits closed on the desk directly between them.

Keep each panel's character designs exactly consistent with the descriptions given. Vary the shot scale and camera angle between panels: mix wide/establishing shots (full body, showing the room), medium shots (waist-up), and close-ups (face or a key object/detail filling most of the frame). Favor dynamic, asymmetric poses and motion over static front-facing standing poses.

ABSOLUTE RULE: do not draw any text, letters, numbers, speech bubbles, thought bubbles, caption boxes, or written characters of any kind anywhere in the image, in any panel. Only the black panel border lines separating the panels are allowed as line art; no other markings.
